# Joint shell signatures: exact-loss equivalence and a partial-information calibration

This note answers an information-sufficiency question for one FIXED
actual deformation and one FIXED critical cap circuit. Full source and
target signatures do not create a new coupling optimization: their
complete loss cost has the already fixed actual cap losses as its
expectation. Retaining only some source signatures gives a valid finite
lower-bound relaxation. Its exact improvement in the five-fiber example
comes from known captured source fibers, not a new transport principle.

## 1. Fixed physical marginals and the full pointwise cost

Consider the actual compatible simultaneous contractions in
`candidate 046287857a52d424`.
For each contracted fiber z, put alpha_z=d|K_z| and let nu_z be its
normalized boundary cone measure about the fixed contraction center.
These laws and coefficients belong to the one specified body variation.
For a finite cap menu H_j, assume its boundaries have nu_z-measure zero.
The actual first-order loss is

    L_j=sum_z alpha_z nu_z(H_j).                         (1)

Fix actual response weights theta_j>=0, sum theta_j=1. They are determined
by the critical circuit's normals and coareas, not by a coupling choice.
Let pi be any coupling of the FULL laws nu_z. It may be restricted by
shared-source conditional gluing or any other additional constraint.
For every sample, record all source bits sigma_zj=1_Hj(z,X_z), and all
target bits tau_Ej for the actual barycentric outputs of the chosen
anchored relations E. Write

    C_theta(sigma)=sum_j theta_j sum_z alpha_z sigma_zj.  (2)

Then, for EVERY such coupling,

    E_pi C_theta=sum_j theta_j L_j.                      (3)

Proof: expand the finite sum and use each fixed source marginal. Only
the one-bit marginals are needed; fixing the complete source signature
laws is already more information than (3) requires. The same conclusion
holds for every finite-support coupling LP and for arbitrary Borel
couplings. No regularity of the transport or target densities enters.

Let B_theta(tau) be any target-signature bound satisfying
B_theta(tau)<=C_theta(sigma) on actual samples. For instance it may be
the minimum hitting-set cost obtained from the affine implications

    tau_Ej=1 implies sum_(z in E) sigma_zj>=1.             (4)

If the FULL actual surplus is retained, define

    D_theta(sigma,tau)=C_theta(sigma)-B_theta(tau)>=0.

Its combined objective is identically

    E_pi[B_theta+D_theta]=sum_j theta_j L_j.              (5)

Thus maximizing the full combined objective over pi is tautological.
Optimizing the surplus alone can change it, but its change is exactly
offset by the target term when both are retained. Restrictions on actual
realizability or on conditional gluing cannot change (5), provided the
admissible family is nonempty. Changing the cap menu can change the
right side, but that is actual row selection with different source
traces, not a coupling gain for a fixed menu.

The fixed regular critical response is consequently

    q_c-beta M' = beta sum_z alpha_z - sum_j theta_j L_j. (6)

Rewriting its last term as (5) neither proves a new sign nor loses data.
This closes the proposed FULL-source-signature optimization route as a
reformulation of known exact cap losses.

## 2. What a selected-source relaxation retains

Choose a subset R of the contracted source fibers. Given their actual
joint signature sigma_R and the target signature tau, define the finite
pointwise cost

    c_R(sigma_R,tau)
      =min C_theta(sigma),                              (7)

where the retained bits are fixed and the omitted bits range over all
Boolean completions satisfying (4). A completion exists because the
actual sample is one. No completion is asserted to be geometrically
realizable; allowing extra completions only weakens this LOWER bound.
For any one actual common coupling,

    E c_R <= sum_j theta_j L_j.                          (8)

This is a finite table calculation once the retained joint law of
(sigma_R,tau) is known. If R increases, the pointwise and expected bounds
increase. For R containing every source, (8) is the equality (3).

One may maximize (8) over actual admissible couplings, retaining full
physical source marginals. This can matter while omitted signature data
are deliberately discarded. It is an information relaxation, however,
and its endpoint at full information is the coupling-independent (3).
An arbitrary finite table satisfying (4) is not automatically the
signature law of an actual coupling; such a relaxation cannot be used
as an attained lower-bound certificate without an actual lift.

## 3. Exact hierarchy for the actual five-fiber deformation

Use Sections 4--5 of the shell source cited above. The fibers at
z=-2,-1,0,1,2 are centered rectangles with halfwidths

    (1,1), (5/2,7/4), (3,2), (5/2,7/4), (1,1).

The total area is67, and the globally critical source is the origin with
beta=1/2. Contract only s=-1, a=1, b=2 about their centers. Their loss
coefficients are

    alpha_s=35, alpha_a=35, alpha_b=8,
    -M'=78, beta(-M')=39.                               (9)

The actual anchored outputs are based on the relations
0=(-1+1)/2=(2/3)(-1)+(1/3)2. A common cone-uniform square boundary
variable Z gives

    Y_1=((5/2)Z_x,(7/4)Z_y),
    Y_2=(2Z_x,(3/2)Z_y).

Use the genuinely critical TILTED circuit

    x+y+10z>=0, -x+y+10z>=0, -y+10z>=0.

Its actual response weights are (3/10,3/10,2/5). At target base0 its
joint target signature law is exactly the same as the cylindrical
critical circuit. In every cap both target probabilities are1/2. Their
intersection is79/160 in the first two caps and1/2 in the third.

The actual source signatures, in contrast, are deterministic:

    sigma_s=(0,0,0), sigma_a=sigma_b=(1,1,1).             (10)

For each cap, if t_1,t_2 are its two target bits, its target-only hitting
cost is35t_1+8t_2-8t_1t_2. Retaining a's captured bit changes the
pointwise lower bound to35+8t_2; retaining b's changes it to8+35t_1.
Retaining s's missed bit forces the two exclusive payments separately,
giving35t_1+8t_2. Retaining both a and b gives43 for every sample.
These are exact Boolean minima in (7), not merely feasible costs.

Consequently the complete eight-subset table is

| Retained sources R | E c_R |
|---|---:|
| empty | 1753/100 |
| s | 43/2 |
| a | 39 |
| b | 51/2 |
| s,a | 39 |
| s,b | 51/2 |
| a,b | 43 |
| s,a,b | 43 |

Thus the selected-source relaxation has an actual strict improvement:
retaining a and b raises the certificate from1753/100 to43, above the
response threshold39. Retaining at most one of these two captured
exclusive sources cannot prove strict descent through this particular
Boolean relaxation, even if the shared source's missed signature is
also retained. The improvement43 is already forced by the two known
positive source marginals; it does not depend on any choice of coupling.

With all source data retained, the exact cylindrical losses are39 in
every cap, and the exact tilted losses are43 in every cap. Hence the
former has neutral first response and the latter strictly negative
normalized response. These actual losses are exactly what (3) recovers.
The cited source separately checks convex compatibility for the specified
one-sided contraction, all-normal global criticality, and persistent slack covers
on the other base planes. In particular the tilt payment is a genuine
strict decrease of the actual global normalized depth under the same
one-sided contraction; it is not a claim about an arbitrary menu.

## 4. Verification and stopping rule

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_joint_shell_signature_information_defect_transport.py` integrates
the actual cone law exactly by splitting its four square faces at every
actual cap crossing, builds the full joint target signature table, and
enumerates all Boolean completions for all eight retained subsets.
It also checks the two exact full-source loss vectors separately.

The full-data objective (5) is therefore parked: it is identically the
known exact critical response, not a new proof mechanism. The subset
table is useful for measuring precisely which source information was
discarded. Its successful tilt payment comes from captured source fibers
whose loss is already known. No global existence or selection theorem
over retained subsets is proposed.
